title: Resolve upstream license grant with joshinryz before publicizing the fork
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)

The fork's license status cannot be settled from inside this repo. Upstream
(joshinryz/volo_discord_bot) publishes no LICENSE file and never has — GitHub
reports licenseInfo:null and `git log -- LICENSE` is empty across its whole
history — while its README asserts "[MIT License](LICENSE)", a link to a file
that does not exist. That is an intent to license without an actual grant, so
the default is all-rights-reserved and this fork cannot pass on rights it never
clearly received.

I removed the inherited MIT claim from our README (7820413) and replaced it with
an accurate "no license granted" statement, plus an Attribution section naming
the upstream authors and itemizing inherited vs original files. That makes the
repo honest, but it does not make it redistributable. Only the copyright holder
can do that, which requires contacting a third party and waiting on their reply
— outside what I can do.

## Current state (updated)

Evan decided NOT to raise licensing in the first contact. The drafted upstream
issue is now a pure courtesy heads-up: the DAVE voice-receive breakage, a
summary of this fork's changes, and an offer of PRs. It deliberately does not
ask for a LICENSE file. Draft: scratchpad/upstream-issue-draft.md (session
499e042a). Opening a friendly channel first is a reasonable play — the license
ask lands better as a follow-up than as an opening demand — but it means this
issue stays OPEN after that message is posted.

## Steps

1. Post the heads-up issue at
   https://github.com/joshinryz/volo_discord_bot/issues/new — review the tone
   first; it is my draft going out under your name.
2. If joshinryz replies and the exchange is friendly, follow up with the license
   question: their README promises MIT but no LICENSE file exists, and adding
   one via GitHub's template picker takes two minutes. Record which license they
   choose.
3. If there is no reply after a few weeks, decide the fallback: leave the repo
   unlicensed and unpublicized, or rewrite/remove the remaining inherited files
   (helper.py, pdf_generator.py, commandline.py, cliargs.py, and
   assets/parchment_background.jpg, whose own provenance is undocumented) so the
   fork no longer depends on the unresolved grant.
4. Close this issue with the outcome recorded.

## What unblocks me when this returns

The upstream license decision, recorded here. If a permissive license is
granted, I add a LICENSE file carrying joshinryz's copyright notice alongside
yours and rewrite the README License section to match. If the answer is no or
silence, I act on your step-3 decision instead.

Still blocking regardless: do not publicize the fork (blog post, Reddit, Discord
communities) until this is closed. Posting the heads-up issue does not resolve
it — that message makes no license ask, so it changes nothing about
redistribution rights.

title: Add upstream attribution; remove unsubstantiated MIT license claim
description: The repo is a fork of joshinryz/volo_discord_bot (history starts at 92ce6d2, 2023-12-20) but carries zero attribution to upstream. It also inherited a README 'License: [MIT License](LICENSE)' line pointing at a LICENSE file that has never existed in either repo — upstream has licenseInfo:null and no LICENSE in its entire history. Publishing a public repo that asserts MIT over derived code with no actual grant is the risk. Fix: credit the fork lineage in README, and drop the license claim until the upstream grant is clarified with the original author.
close_reason: README attribution + honest license statement landed in 7820413. Attribution section names Josh Robinett and Noah Feinberg, records fork point 5e610b2, and itemizes inherited vs original files; License section now states no grant until upstream is resolved. Verified README was the only place in the tree making a license claim. Preflight green (258 tests). Upstream license resolution tracked separately.

title: Capture per-speaker session audio to disk so a live session yields A/B reference data
description: 3dn (the gating human step for the whole accuracy epic) needs per-speaker WAV clips + a reference transcript + a JSONL manifest. Today WhisperSink transcribes audio and discards it — the raw bytes are never written anywhere — so a live session produces a transcript but NO reference clips, and 3dn stays blocked no matter how many sessions are played. Add an env-gated capture mode that persists the EXACT wav bytes the sink feeds the backend, plus a draft manifest pre-filled with the machine transcription, so the human step collapses from 'transcribe hours of audio from scratch' to 'correct a draft'.
acceptance_criteria: CAPTURE_SESSION_AUDIO=1 writes per-speaker clips + manifest.draft.jsonl under captures/<session>/; manifest is consumable by scripts/ab_transcribe.py --manifest after human correction; capture failures never break transcription; disk-usage cap; off by default; unit tests cover clip+manifest write, disabled-by-default, and failure isolation; make preflight passes.
close_reason: Implemented in 059128d: src/session_capture.py (clips + manifest.draft.jsonl + session_info.json + README, thread-safe, disk-capped, never raises into the transcription path), wired into WhisperSink behind CAPTURE_SESSION_AUDIO (off by default), make capture-session/prewarm targets, ab_transcribe .draft guard, captures/ gitignored. 20 new tests (244 total); preflight green. Verified end-to-end with the real MLX backend via scripts/smoke_capture.py: 3 synthetic speakers -> clips -> draft manifest -> corrected -> harness scored WER 5.6% / RTF 0.23.

title: Roster -> initial_prompt proper-noun biasing
description: Feed character/player/place names from player_map.yml into faster-whisper's initial_prompt so the model spells D&D proper nouns correctly (e.g. Arasaka, Night City, character names). This is the cheapest high-leverage accuracy win and exploits data we already load. initial_prompt is end-weighted and capped ~224 tokens, so build the hint from the active session's roster (bounded), not the whole map. Touches src/sinks/whisper_sink.py (transcribe_audio) + the player_map already passed to WhisperSink.
acceptance_criteria: WhisperSink builds an initial_prompt from the session roster names (deduped, length-bounded to a safe token budget) and passes it to audio_model.transcribe; falls back to the existing generic D&D prompt when no roster; unit test asserts roster names appear in the prompt and the budget cap is enforced.
close_reason: Implemented in ee30411: roster names appended to initial_prompt (deduped, char-first, budget-bounded), both backends, 5 tests. A/B validation on real audio tracked by discord-transcript-bot-61z.

title: Research-driven transcription accuracy + performance upgrades
description: Umbrella for the accuracy-first improvements identified by the 2026-06-09 deep-research cycle (faster-whisper/Whisper-family + non-Whisper ASR on Apple Silicon primary, CPU-only fallback). Goal: better WER on noisy, overlapping, proper-noun-heavy D&D speech while staying near-realtime. Key validated insights: (a) Discord per-user streams already sidestep diarization — keep that architecture; (b) highest-leverage accuracy win is contextual vocabulary biasing from the existing roster; (c) on Apple Silicon, GPU/ANE backends (MLX-Whisper, whisper.cpp+CoreML, Parakeet/CoreML) are ~6-7x faster than CPU faster-whisper; (d) streaming adds a ~1.9s algorithmic latency floor so it's deprioritized. All WER/RTFx figures are from clean benchmarks and MUST be A/B tested on real session audio before committing.

title: WhisperSink transcription backlog snowballs under heavy multi-speaker load
description: Live session 2026-06-09: transcript writes lagged 6+ min and grew unbounded during a busy 5-speaker combat scene. Root cause is two compounding factors: (1) large-v3 at compute_type=float32 on CPU is the slowest/most-RAM-hungry faster-whisper config (RSS hit ~9.6GB), throughput < real-time; (2) insert_voice blocks on future.result() each pass, so it stops draining voice_queue while a multi-minute segment transcribes -> queue piles up -> next per-speaker segment is even longer -> positive feedback loop. No per-speaker segment-length cap, so one speaker's buffer grew to ~6 min of audio. Not a crash; no data lost (unbounded queue). Fix: int8 precision on CPU, cap per-speaker segment duration with a force-flush, and detach transcription from the drain loop (submit + done-callback instead of blocking future.result()).
acceptance_criteria: int8 on CPU; per-speaker buffer force-flushed past a duration cap; insert_voice keeps draining voice_queue while a transcribe future is outstanding (queue depth stays bounded under sustained input); tests cover the cap and the non-blocking drain; make preflight passes.
close_reason: Fix landed and merged to main (PR #1): int8 on CPU (src/asr/selection.py), MAX_SEGMENT_S=30 force-flush cap + detached non-blocking drain (src/sinks/whisper_sink.py); tests test_buffer_force_flushed_past_duration_cap and test_drain_continues_while_a_transcription_is_in_flight cover both. Live-load re-verification happens naturally next session; heartbeat/stall watchdog (5060b3b) will surface any recurrence.

title: Move /ask to OpenRouter primary + Cerebras paid fallback, Ollama last resort
description: /ask is local-Ollama-only, which ties transcript Q&A to a warm 26B model on the host. Move it to the provider chain used in raylytics/louisville-open-data-expenditure-bot: OpenRouter primary, Cerebras paid fallback, both via the OpenAI-compatible client already in requirements. Port the classifier/fallback semantics from analytics_agent.py (402 + free-models-per-day 429 cross over immediately and latch the primary out for 15 min; ordinary 429 gets one more primary attempt first; empty completion fails over). Keep Ollama as a third, last-resort local tier so /ask survives offline or with both keys dry. Also fix the pre-existing event-loop block: ollama.chat ran synchronously inside the async command, and a cloud call chain would stall the bot far longer.
close_reason: Landed in d88e344. src/llm/{config,errors,chain}.py implement OpenRouter -> Cerebras paid -> Ollama with the reference repo's classifier semantics (402/daily-cap latch + cross over, ordinary 429 retries once without latching, empty/404 fail over, user message from the first tier's error). main.py calls it via asyncio.to_thread, fixing the pre-existing event-loop block. health.py gains a non-critical ask_providers check. 31 new tests; preflight green at 289. Live-verified the real SDK path and failover against Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint; paid keys not yet in .env so the cloud endpoints themselves are unexercised.

title: Marginal-audio decodes are order-dependent — bake-off must exclude near-unintelligible clips
description:
Measured 2026-08-11 on real captured clips with the production MLX backend. For LOW-QUALITY audio, transcription output depends on what was transcribed earlier in the same process: clip 0019 decoded as 'Do we follow up with those?' when transcribed alone in a fresh process, but 'Thank you for being a follow-up.' when one other clip was transcribed first. Repeats WITHIN a process are stable (3/3 identical), so this is not random per-call noise — it is MLX GPU numerical state flipping a marginal argmax.

CLEAR speech is NOT affected: clip 0009 produced byte-identical text alone vs after two other clips. condition_on_previous_text is already False, so that is not the cause.

Consequences for the A/B harness (3dn/d6j): run_config loops every clip through one process, so marginal clips contribute WER that depends on clip order and on which config ran first. Differences between configs on such clips are noise, not signal.

Mitigation: exclude near-unintelligible clips from the reference manifest (delete rather than guess — the capture README already says not to leave an empty reference). Optionally have ab_transcribe report per-clip WER variance, or run each config in a fresh subprocess, so order effects are visible rather than silently folded into the corpus number.
acceptance_criteria: Bake-off methodology documented so marginal clips can't silently skew results; ideally ab_transcribe surfaces per-clip variance or isolates configs.
close_reason: ab_transcribe: per-clip WER, --order-trials flags order-sensitive clips, --stable-manifest excludes them, --isolate runs configs in fresh subprocesses; methodology in capture README + CLAUDE.md; 10 new tests

title: [bug] Bot burns 100% of one CPU core continuously while connected/recording
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)

Everything that can be done offline is done and committed (6494999): the spin is
scoped to a thread Pycord starts only while recording; the packet router was
cleared by reproduction (0.00 CPU-s in six scenarios); `UDPKeepAlive.run` was found
to retry a failed UDP send with no delay (~6.5k iterations/s, DEBUG-only log) and is
now patched with a guarded 1s backoff + WARNING logging; `kill -USR1 <pid>` writes a
ranked thread dump; `bot_state.json` carries `cpu_pct` and the heartbeat warns when
hot-and-idle. What I cannot do: (a) confirm the keep-alive is the live culprit — that
needs a real recording session on this Mac, and no logs from 2026-08-11 survive
(`discord` was at WARNING, the relevant messages were DEBUG); (b) post the upstream
report — it goes out under your GitHub account on a third party's PR.

## Steps

1. Next live session (`make capture-session` or `make start`), after `/connect` +
   `/scribe`, watch `.logs/bot_state.json` → `cpu_pct` (refreshes every 30s), or
   `top -pid $(pgrep -f 'python main.py')`. The heartbeat now logs a WARNING by
   itself if CPU ≥ 90% while nothing is queued and nothing was transcribed for 60s.
2. If it spins: `kill -USR1 $(pgrep -f 'python main.py')`. Read
   `.logs/thread_dump-<ts>.txt` — the top entry is the moving thread. Paste the
   top two entries into this issue. Also grep the terminal for
   "Voice UDP keep-alive send failed" — if present, the diagnosis is confirmed and
   the errno in that line is the root cause.
3. If it does NOT spin across a full session with the patch in place, note that
   here too — that is evidence for the keep-alive theory (the patch bounded it).
4. Post the upstream report: review `docs/upstream/pycord-udp-keepalive-spin.md`
   (it includes a no-Discord reproduction) and post it as a review comment on
   https://github.com/Pycord-Development/pycord/pull/3159 or a new issue. Adjust tone;
   it is my draft going out under your name. Record the URL here.
5. When #3159 merges into a 2.9.0 release (see the DAVE note in CLAUDE.md): re-check
   `UDPKeepAlive.run` — if fixed upstream, delete `src/bot/pycord_patches.py`, its
   test, and the CLAUDE.md bullet.

## What unblocks me when this returns

Either (a) the thread-dump excerpt + any "keep-alive send failed" line (I then
finalise the diagnosis, and, if the culprit is a different thread, patch that path the
same guarded way), or (b) "ran a full session, no spin" (I close this as mitigated),
plus the upstream report URL for the CLAUDE.md note.

## Prior description (preserved on handoff)

Observed 2026-08-11 on the live capture session (PID 26924, 'make capture-session'). Measured instantaneously, not from ps's lifetime average: process CPU time advanced 10.00s over 10s of wall clock = exactly one core pegged, sustained 39+ minutes while the room was silent and queue_depth was 0.

State at the time (.logs/bot_state.json): recording=true, queue_depth=0, stalled=false, output_age=2058s. So it spins while connected+recording with NO audio arriving.

RULED OUT — the transcription engine. A process that imports src.asr.selection, loads the MLX backend and runs a transcription, then idles, consumes 0.00 CPU-s over 10s wall (0%). So it is not MLX/Metal, torch/OpenMP, or model residency.

REMAINING SUSPECTS: (a) Pycord's voice-receive loop on the fix/voice-rec-2 DAVE branch — the most likely, since the spin correlates with being connected; (b) WhisperSink.insert_voice, whose time.sleep(IDLE_SLEEP_S) sits INSIDE the try block, so any exception raised each iteration skips the sleep and hot-loops while logging 'Error in insert_voice' every pass.

NEXT DIAGNOSTIC: run /stop (sink closes, voice thread exits, voice client stays connected) and re-measure; then /disconnect and re-measure. That separates (a) from (b) in two steps. Also check the operator's terminal for an 'Error in insert_voice' flood, which would immediately confirm (b). py-spy would name the exact frame but requires root on macOS.

WHY IT MATTERS: a full core for a 4-hour session is real heat/battery, and on a busy machine it competes with the transcription thread pool — the same resource pressure behind the -hin backlog snowball.

CHEAP HARDENING REGARDLESS: move insert_voice's sleep into a finally, so no exception path can ever produce a hot loop.
acceptance_criteria: Idle CPU while connected+recording with no audio is near 0%. If insert_voice is implicated, its sleep is unconditional so an exception cannot hot-loop.
notes:
2026-08-30 (agent): offline root-cause work done, live confirmation pending.
- Scope: SocketReader/PacketRouter/SinkEventRouter/SpeakingTimer/UDPKeepAlive are the recording-only threads (SocketReader only runs while a listener is registered) — matches 'stops on /stop while connected'.
- PacketRouter+PacketDecoder+JitterBuffer+MultiDataEvent driven with real RTPPacket bytes: clean burst / packet loss / resume / duplicate / destroy_decoder / tail loss all = 0.00 CPU-s per 2s of silence. Router cleared.
- UDPKeepAlive.run: on ANY sendto exception -> wait_until_connected() (instant while connected) -> `continue`, no sleep. Measured ~6.5k iterations/s with a failing sendto. Logged only at DEBUG (bot runs discord at WARNING => invisible). Also delay=5000 used as SECONDS (keep-alive every 83 min; uninterruptible sleep). Persistent sendto failure while 'connected' is realistic on macOS (EADDRNOTAVAIL after local-IP change; ENETUNREACH during a blip).
- Same code on branch head cb46392 (2026-08-29) as on the pinned a61fdc9; PR #3159 still open, milestone 2.9.0. No existing upstream issue found.
- Landed (6494999): src/bot/pycord_patches.py guarded backoff+WARNING; src/utils/thread_dump.py (kill -USR1 -> .logs/thread_dump-*.txt); cpu_pct in bot_state.json + hot-and-idle heartbeat warning; docs/upstream/pycord-udp-keepalive-spin.md draft.
- Not the cause but noted: JitterBuffer pref_size=1 holds the last packet of every burst until the speaker's next packet (20ms tail delivered with the next utterance).

title: /ask is broken: DEFAULT_ASK_MODEL 'ai/mistral:latest' is unpullable, and health.py recommends the failing command
description:
Confirmed live 2026-08-11 19:20 in Discord: /ask returned "model 'ai/mistral:latest' not found (status code: 404)".

Root cause: 'ai/' is Docker Hub's namespace for Docker Model Runner, not Ollama's. Verified against Ollama's registry — registry.ollama.ai/v2/ai/mistral/manifests/latest returns 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN, while library/mistral:latest returns 200. So DEFAULT_ASK_MODEL in src/config/ollama_config.py can never be pulled by Ollama, and src/bot/health.py's warning tells the user to run 'ollama pull ai/mistral:latest', which fails the same way. Docker is installed on this host but Model Runner is not running, so nothing serves that name either. The local Ollama store is also completely empty (ollama list = 0 models).

This was already documented as a latent bug in the sibling local-models repo (dev/discord-ask-model/README.md, 'Registry finding'), whose bake-off also settled the model choice: gemma4:26b won decisively (6/6 human-judged correct, sub-600ms median) vs mistral:latest (3/6 — misattributed a death save to Johan when the transcript says Cody, and conflated separate threads into a hallucinated summary). The winner was never promoted into the bot.
acceptance_criteria: DEFAULT_ASK_MODEL is a name Ollama can actually pull; health.py's remediation message suggests a command that works; /ask answers successfully against the benchmarked model. Note the bot reads ASK_OLLAMA_MODEL per call via get_ask_model() but from the process env, so a .env change needs a bot restart.
close_reason: Fixed in 2733ca0. DEFAULT_ASK_MODEL is now gemma4:26b (bake-off winner); is_ollama_pullable() stops health.py recommending an impossible pull; CLAUDE.md/.env.sample updated; a test asserts the default is pullable so the bug class can't return. Verified end-to-end after pulling gemma4:26b (17GB): get_ask_model() resolves it and ollama.chat with the bot's exact params (think=False, num_predict=512, temperature=0) returns a correct grounded answer AND a clean refusal on an out-of-transcript question, at 0.59-0.70s warm — matching the benchmark's 573ms p50. Requires a bot restart to take effect (ASK_OLLAMA_MODEL is bound at main.py import).

title: Capture a recorded D&D session + reference transcript for the transcription A/B harness
description:
## Why
Every remaining accuracy decision (d6j model/beam bake-off, mni Parakeet, 1s7 VAD) is
gated on scoring configs against REAL session audio. Leaderboard WER is clean speech and
may not transfer to noisy, overlapping, proper-noun-heavy D&D. The harness
(scripts/ab_transcribe.py) is built and waiting on reference data.

## This got much easier (2026-08-11, discord-transcript-bot-h7j)
The bot can now capture its own reference data. Previously this task meant recording a
session by hand and transcribing hours of audio from scratch. Now a capture-enabled
session writes the per-speaker clips AND a draft manifest pre-filled with the machine
transcription — so the human step is CORRECTING a draft, not producing one.

## Runbook
1. Warm the model first (cold cache = ~3GB download that stalls startup):
     make prewarm
2. Run the session with capture on:
     make capture-session          # == CAPTURE_SESSION_AUDIO=1 python main.py
   Then /connect + /scribe as usual and play. Everything else behaves normally.
3. Afterwards look in captures/<session-timestamp>/ — per-speaker .wav clips,
   manifest.draft.jsonl, and a README with the correction workflow.
4. Correct the reference text. Open manifest.draft.jsonl, play each clip, fix the
   'reference' field to what was ACTUALLY said — especially character/player names,
   which are the whole point of the proper-noun work. Lines flagged needs_reference:true
   had their transcription dropped: type the real words or delete the line (never leave
   an empty reference; it skews corpus WER). You do NOT need to correct everything —
   a few hundred seconds spanning all speakers, including noisy/overlapping moments and
   plenty of spoken names, beats hours of clean solo narration.
5. Save it as manifest.jsonl (drop the .draft) and verify:
     python scripts/ab_transcribe.py --manifest captures/<session>/manifest.jsonl
   It should print per-config WER + RTF. The harness warns loudly if handed an
   uncorrected .draft file, because scoring against machine text measures nothing.
6. Bounce back to the agent — this unblocks d6j, mni and 1s7.

## Disk
~192 KB per second of captured speech (48kHz/16-bit/stereo, the exact bytes fed to the
engine). A long session with several talkative players runs to a few GB; capture stops
at CAPTURE_MAX_GB (default 20) rather than filling the disk.

title: Wire MLX backend into A/B harness + run model/beam bake-off on real session audio
description: Extend scripts/ab_transcribe.py _transcribe_clip with an mlx-whisper backend branch (reusing src/asr/mlx_backend.MlxWhisperBackend) and add MLX configs to DEFAULT_CONFIGS. Then run the bake-off on a real recorded D&D session (multi-speaker, noisy, proper-noun-heavy) scored with src/wer.py to settle the still-open accuracy decisions: large-v3 vs large-v3-turbo, and beam_size 5 vs 10 (the std issue lowered beam 10->5 purely for CPU cost; the MLX GPU removes that constraint, so re-evaluate). Lock the final WHISPER_MODEL and WHISPER_BEAM_SIZE defaults from the measured numbers, not a guess. Blocked on a captured reference session (see linked human task).
acceptance_criteria: ab_transcribe.py dispatches on cfg.backend=='mlx-whisper'; DEFAULT_CONFIGS includes MLX large-v3 at beam5 and beam10; bake-off run produces per-config WER+RTF on real session audio; final WHISPER_MODEL/WHISPER_BEAM_SIZE chosen and documented from the numbers; test_ab_transcribe.py covers MLX dispatch (mocked).
notes: Code half DONE (commit 49c6b50): scripts/ab_transcribe.py now has the mlx-whisper dispatch (reuses src/asr/mlx_backend) + MLX large-v3/turbo configs; test_mlx_backend_dispatches covers routing. REMAINING (gated on 3dn reference audio): run the bake-off on real session audio and lock final WHISPER_MODEL. NOTE: mlx_whisper is greedy-only (no beam search), so the beam5-vs-beam10 comparison applies only to faster-whisper rows; MLX accuracy levers are model id + temperature.

title: A/B accuracy harness on real session audio
description: Validation infrastructure: capture/replay real multi-speaker session audio and score WER across engine/param configs, since all research benchmarks are clean-speech and may not transfer to noisy D&D. Enables data-driven decisions for VAD swap, Parakeet bake-off, and decode tuning. Likely needs a recorded session with a reference transcript (human step).
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable script under scripts/ that runs N configs over the same recorded audio and emits per-config WER + RTF; documented how to supply reference audio/transcript.
close_reason: Harness built + tested (src/wer.py + scripts/ab_transcribe.py, 14 tests, no new deps). Emits per-config WER+RTF over single audio or a per-speaker manifest. Ready to run once a recorded session + reference transcript is supplied; that run happens under the turbo decision (d29) and the VAD/Parakeet bake-offs (1s7/mni), which are now unblocked.

title: Add BatchedInferencePipeline to CPU fallback
description: Wrap the faster-whisper CPU path in BatchedInferencePipeline for extra throughput at no precision change. Biggest benefit on the 30s MAX_SEGMENT_S force-flushed segments (VAD-chunked + batched); short utterances see less. Measure peak RAM (batching raises it). Touches src/sinks/whisper_sink.py transcribe_audio.
acceptance_criteria: CPU backend uses BatchedInferencePipeline with a tuned batch_size; transcription output unchanged in content; a smoke/benchmark note records wall-clock + peak RAM vs current int8 unbatched.
close_reason: Implemented: std=configurable beam/best_of (default 5/5) in bd510ad; ob3=BatchedInferencePipeline CPU wrapper in the latest commit. Both code-only, tests green. Speed/accuracy values to be A/B-validated on real audio by discord-transcript-bot-61z.

title: Runtime ASR backend selector + MLX-Whisper (Apple Silicon primary)
description: Introduce a transcription-backend abstraction selected at runtime: Apple Silicon -> MLX-Whisper (Metal, ~6-7x faster than CPU); otherwise -> existing CPU int8 faster-whisper fallback. Must degrade gracefully on non-Apple/older hardware (the hard fallback requirement). Keep the per-user-stream + ordered-commit pipeline unchanged; only the transcribe() inference call swaps. Optionally evaluate whisper.cpp+CoreML (ANE) as an alternative primary.
design: Backend abstraction lives in new package src/asr/ (base.py defines a NormalizedSegment dataclass + TranscribeResult + TranscriptionBackend ABC; faster_whisper_backend.py, mlx_backend.py, selection.py). CRITICAL: the two existing accuracy layers must survive the swap unchanged — (1) the per-segment hallucination filter WhisperSink._accept_segment reads seg.text/no_speech_prob/avg_logprob/compression_ratio, and (2) roster initial_prompt biasing (_build_initial_prompt + _is_prompt_echo). Every backend MUST yield segment objects exposing those four fields (via NormalizedSegment); MLX-Whisper supports initial_prompt so layer 2 is preserved. _normalize_mlx maps MLX result segments -> NormalizedSegment, failing OPEN per missing field (defaults that keep the segment: no_speech_prob=0.0, avg_logprob=0.0, compression_ratio=1.0, matching _accept_segment getattr defaults) with one WARN, so missing metrics never silently drop real speech. selection.get_backend() is memoized so health.py + the sink share one model load. Open risks: verify mlx_whisper segments actually carry those metrics; verify MLX thread-safety under the ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8) (serialize/cap if not); MLX has no Silero VAD (relies on Whisper no_speech gating + _accept_segment).
acceptance_criteria: A backend interface with at least faster-whisper-CPU and MLX-Whisper implementations; auto-selects MLX on Apple Silicon and falls back to faster-whisper elsewhere (selection never raises); selection overridable by env (ASR_BACKEND); insert_voice/ordered-commit path untouched; new backends yield segment objects carrying text/no_speech_prob/avg_logprob/compression_ratio so the hallucination filter AND roster initial_prompt biasing both still apply regardless of backend; health.py updated to ping the selected backend; tests cover selection logic with both backends mocked AND assert both accuracy layers apply to normalized segments; make preflight passes.
close_reason: Implemented in src/asr/ (commit 0ba9eb4): backend abstraction + MLX-Whisper w/ graceful faster-whisper fallback, accuracy-first large-v3 default, NormalizedSegment preserves both accuracy layers, health.py pings selected backend, env docs added (dca7dc7). 224 tests pass; preflight green (live graceful fallback to faster-whisper verified on this arm64 host w/o mlx_whisper).

title: Make Whisper model configurable; default large-v3 (accuracy-first)
description: Add WHISPER_MODEL env/config. Default to large-v3 (most accurate Whisper) rather than turbo: the goal is accuracy-first, and the MLX GPU backend (d8g) makes large-v3 affordable in near-realtime, so we keep the most accurate model and spend the GPU headroom on accuracy (higher beam, no int8 quantization loss) instead of trading down. Keep large-v3-turbo selectable via env for CPU/speed-constrained hosts. Update health check + CLAUDE.md env docs. Touches src/sinks/whisper_sink.py model load (moving into src/asr/selection.py per d8g) + src/bot/health.py whisper_model check.
acceptance_criteria: Model id read from env (WHISPER_MODEL) with default large-v3; large-v3-turbo still selectable; health check reports the configured model; CLAUDE.md env docs updated.
close_reason: Implemented in src/asr/ (commit 0ba9eb4): backend abstraction + MLX-Whisper w/ graceful faster-whisper fallback, accuracy-first large-v3 default, NormalizedSegment preserves both accuracy layers, health.py pings selected backend, env docs added (dca7dc7). 224 tests pass; preflight green (live graceful fallback to faster-whisper verified on this arm64 host w/o mlx_whisper).

title: Bare 'Thank you' may be an unfiltered Whisper silence hallucination (seen twice in first real capture)
description:
First real capture (captures/2026-08-11_19-19-01) produced 'Thank you.' (clip 0003) and 'Thank you!' (clip 0025) — the two shortest non-empty segments, both ~1.2s, RMS 477 and 619. Bare 'thank you' is a well-known Whisper silence-hallucination artifact, but _HALLUCINATION_PHRASES in src/sinks/whisper_sink.py only contains the longer variants ('thank you for watching', 'thanks for watching', ...), so it passes the filter.

NOT yet proven: RMS alone doesn't settle it. Real speech was transcribed at comparable levels in the same session (clip 0021 RMS 402, clip 0019 RMS 339), so low level is not sufficient evidence. Settle it by listening to clips 0003 and 0025 in that capture directory.

DO NOT blindly add 'thank you' to _HALLUCINATION_PHRASES: unlike 'thanks for watching', it is a phrase people genuinely say at a table, so filtering it would silently delete real speech — the failure mode the conservative-defaults comment in whisper_sink.py warns about. If confirmed, prefer gating on the segment metrics (no_speech_prob/avg_logprob) for short segments rather than a blanket phrase match.
acceptance_criteria: Listen to clips 0003/0025 and decide; if hallucinated, implement a fix that cannot drop a genuine spoken 'thank you' (metric-gated, not a bare phrase match), with a test covering both directions.
close_reason:
Investigated with the real backend on the actual clips; NOT a phrase-filter problem, so no filter change made.

(1) The metrics cannot separate them. 0003 'Thank you.' scored no_speech_prob 0.228 / avg_logprob -0.923, and 0025 scored 0.370 / -0.909 — statistically indistinguishable from CONFIRMED real speech in the same session (0015 'What happened here?' = 0.245 / -0.903; 0019 = 0.264 / -0.874). The metric-gating fix proposed in this issue therefore cannot work: any threshold that drops the 'Thank you' clips also drops real speech.

(2) The real mechanism is decode instability on marginal audio, not a canned hallucination phrase. Same clip + same params + fresh process yields different text depending only on what was transcribed BEFORE it (clip 0019: 'Do we follow up with those?' alone vs 'Thank you for being a follow-up.' after one other clip). Clear speech is unaffected — clip 0009 was byte-identical across orderings.

So bare 'thank you' must NOT be added to _HALLUCINATION_PHRASES: it is a phrase people genuinely say, the metrics do not justify it, and the underlying cause is decode instability on near-unintelligible audio. Correct handling is to DELETE such clips from a reference manifest rather than guess at them. Split out as its own issue for the bake-off methodology.

title: No startup confirmation that CAPTURE_SESSION_AUDIO is armed
description: The capture directory is created lazily on the first clip, so SessionCapture's 'writing to <dir>' log line doesn't appear until someone speaks — and the sink isn't even constructed until /scribe. Starting the bot with 'make capture-session' therefore looks identical to a normal start (observed 2026-08-11 19:14). The operator's only confirmation is the /scribe reply notice, which is late and easy to miss. Log a line at sink construction (or at bot startup) stating capture is enabled and where it will write.
acceptance_criteria: Starting the bot with CAPTURE_SESSION_AUDIO=1 produces a log line confirming capture is armed, before any audio arrives.
close_reason: Sink now logs 'Session audio capture ENABLED — per-speaker clips will be written to <dir>' at construction, before any audio arrives. Two tests cover it firing when enabled and staying silent when not.

title: Health check should report a cold model cache instead of silently downloading 3GB at startup
description: health.py:_check_whisper_model calls get_backend() + healthcheck(), which on a cold HuggingFace cache triggers a ~3GB download inside the startup health check. The bot looks hung for minutes with no indication why — observed 2026-08-11 when ~/.cache/huggingface was empty. scripts/prewarm_models.py (make prewarm) is the workaround, but health should detect the cold cache first and say so (or at least log 'downloading model weights, this may take several minutes').
acceptance_criteria: Starting the bot with an empty model cache produces a clear log/health message about the download before it begins, rather than an unexplained multi-minute stall.
close_reason: health warns before a cold-cache download (src/asr/model_cache.py); prewarm --check exits 1 when cold; tests in tests/test_model_cache.py + test_health.py

title: Parakeet (CoreML/MLX) accuracy bake-off vs large-v3
description: Spike: evaluate NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT-0.6b (CoreML via FluidAudio or MLX) against faster-whisper large-v3 on REAL session audio. Leaderboard says Parakeet beats large-v3 (6.32 vs 7.44 WER) and is far faster, but that's clean speech and English-only; verify on noisy D&D and check hotword/biasing support before adopting. Uses the A/B harness.
acceptance_criteria: WER + RTF for Parakeet vs large-v3 on real session audio; go/no-go recommendation with notes on English-only + proper-noun biasing support.

title: VAD Silero v4 -> v5/v6 A/B evaluation
description: Silero v5/v6 score higher ROC-AUC than v4, BUT production reports (faster-whisper #934) say v5 can drop more speech. Do NOT blind-swap; A/B v4 vs v5 vs v6 on real session audio via the harness, optimizing for speech retention on noisy/overlapping input. Touches vad_parameters in src/sinks/whisper_sink.py.
acceptance_criteria: Measured comparison of v4/v5/v6 on real session audio; chosen version backed by speech-retention + WER numbers, not just ROC-AUC.

title: Tune decode params (beam_size 10->5, sampling)
description: Current beam_size=10/best_of=3 is unusually high and costly. Lower beam_size to ~5 (faster-whisper default) and reassess best_of/temperature for the accuracy/speed knee on real session audio. Touches src/sinks/whisper_sink.py transcribe_audio.
acceptance_criteria: beam_size/best_of made configurable with sane defaults; an A/B note on real session audio justifies the chosen values (no meaningful WER regression vs beam_size=10).
close_reason: Implemented: std=configurable beam/best_of (default 5/5) in bd510ad; ob3=BatchedInferencePipeline CPU wrapper in the latest commit. Both code-only, tests green. Speed/accuracy values to be A/B-validated on real audio by discord-transcript-bot-61z.
